title: Vestfold Hills: sight lines and midnight sun
text: One data source covers continent. ’s GDAL VRT 2 m REMA tiles overviews 10 m, 32 m, 100 m, 500 m 1 km. GDAL’s warper picks right level resolution asked reads bytes needs, 40 km box 20 m costs small box full detail. source drives browser explorer, https://mdsumner.github.io/rema-ovr/. read_ds() gives heights georeferencing attached, ximage aspersions take directly. Heights run sea level hills kilometre ice sheet, greys spread evenly heights present rather range:
code: dsn #> [1] "/vsicurl/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdsumner/rema-ovr/main/REMA-2m_dem_ovr.vrt" ## the full-resolution levels live in a public bucket, read without credentials set_config_option("AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST", "YES")  ## warp a box of REMA in Antarctic polar stereographic (EPSG:3031) at `res` metres read_rema <- function(extent, res) {   tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")   warp(dsn, tf, t_srs = "EPSG:3031",        cl_arg = c("-te", extent[1], extent[3], extent[2], extent[4], "-tr", res, res, "-r", "bilinear"),        quiet = TRUE)   ds <- new(GDALRaster, tf)   on.exit(ds$close())   read_ds(ds) }  davis <- c(2302286, 490792)                        # Davis station, EPSG:3031 box <- c(2289000, 2330000, 462000, 503000)        # the Vestfold Hills, 41 km square vh <- read_rema(box, 20) attr(vh, "gis")$dim #> [1] 2050 2050    1 relief <- grey.colors(64, 0.15, 0.95) rb <- unique(quantile(vh, seq(0, 1, length.out = 65), na.rm = TRUE)) ximage(vh, col = relief[seq_len(length(rb) - 1)], breaks = rb, asp = 1, axes = FALSE) points(davis[1], davis[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4)

what: What can be seen from a hill near the station
title: Vestfold Hills: sight lines and midnight sun
text: Take highest ground within 3 km Davis stand , eye 2 m.  smooth surface north-east sea. filled REMA used heights , hill coast can see long way across , much gold open water. land, visible ground breaks along ridges fjords hills. skyline lookout comes calculation:
code: z <- matrix(vh, attr(vh, "gis")$dim[2], byrow = TRUE) ex <- attr(vh, "gis")$bbox[c(1, 3, 2, 4)] xs <- seq(ex[1] + 10, by = 20, length.out = ncol(z)) ys <- seq(ex[4] - 10, by = -20, length.out = nrow(z)) d <- sqrt(outer((ys - davis[2])^2, (xs - davis[1])^2, "+")) k <- which(d < 3000 & z == max(z[d < 3000], na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ] lookout <- c(xs[k[2]], ys[k[1]]) lookout #> [1] 2300490  489530 z[k[1], k[2]] #> [1] 87.28956  v <- viewshed(vh, xy = lookout, eye = 2, pieces = FALSE) v #> <aspersions viewshed> #>   eye at (2300490.0, 489530.0), height 89.3 #>   visible: 644,100,000 m^2 from 3,281,192 of 8,396,802 triangles #>   40.7% of the grid visible #>   skyline: -0.4 to 0.9 degrees ximage(vh, col = relief[seq_len(length(rb) - 1)], breaks = rb, asp = 1, axes = FALSE) ximage(v$visible, extent = v$extent, add = TRUE,        col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("gold", 0.7)), breaks = c(-1, 0.01, 2)) points(lookout[1], lookout[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4) par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)) plot(v$skyline, type = "l", xaxt = "n", xlab = "azimuth (degrees from grid north)",      ylab = "horizon (degrees)") axis(1, at = seq(0, 360, by = 90)) abline(h = 0, lty = 3)

what: In detail: 2 m near the lookout
title: Vestfold Hills: sight lines and midnight sun
text: full-resolution tiles come source. 4 km square around lookout read 2 m, 20 m grid behind terrain . near grid four million cells, eight million triangles. visible polygons aren’t needed , pieces = FALSE skips collecting .
code: near_box <- c(lookout[1] - 2000, lookout[1] + 2000, lookout[2] - 2000, lookout[2] + 2000) near <- read_rema(near_box, 2) vn <- viewshed(near, xy = lookout, eye = 2, far = z, far_extent = ex, pieces = FALSE) vn #> <aspersions viewshed> #>   eye at (2300490.0, 489530.0), height 90.1 #>   visible: 647,600,000 m^2 from 5,794,800 of 16,308,804 triangles #>   31.3% of the grid visible #>   skyline: -0.4 to 1.0 degrees nb <- unique(quantile(near, seq(0, 1, length.out = 65), na.rm = TRUE)) ximage(near, col = relief[seq_len(length(nb) - 1)], breaks = nb, asp = 1, axes = FALSE) ximage(vn$visible, extent = vn$extent, add = TRUE,        col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("gold", 0.7)), breaks = c(-1, 0.01, 2)) points(lookout[1], lookout[2], pch = 21, bg = "orangered", cex = 1.4)

title: Vestfold Hills: sight lines and midnight sun
text: Davis 68.6 degrees south, inside Antarctic Circle: around midsummer sun doesn’t set, around midwinter doesn’t rise. Polar stereographic grid north isn’t true north. point, true north points directly away pole, grid azimuth true north longitude, 78 degrees . ’s convergence argument. local midnight midsummer’s day sun low south, hills throw long shadows:  whole day 24 hours daylight. Terrain takes away, valleys slopes facing pole:
code: lonlat <- c(77.967, -68.577) times <- as.POSIXct("2026-12-21 00:00", tz = "Antarctica/Davis") + (0:23) * 3600 round(sun_position(times, lonlat[1], lonlat[2])$elevation, 1) #>  [1]  4.2  2.7  2.3  3.2  5.4  8.6 12.8 17.7 23.0 28.5 33.7 38.4 42.1 44.3 44.8 #> [16] 43.5 40.5 36.4 31.4 26.0 20.5 15.4 10.8  7.0 p <- sun_position(as.POSIXct("2026-12-21 00:00", tz = "Antarctica/Davis"), lonlat[1], lonlat[2]) p #>    azimuth elevation #> 1 204.1893  4.211629 s <- cast_shade(vh, azimuth = p$azimuth, elevation = p$elevation, convergence = lonlat[1]) ximage(vh, col = relief[seq_len(length(rb) - 1)], breaks = rb, asp = 1, axes = FALSE) ximage(s * 1, extent = attr(s, "extent"), add = TRUE, col = c("transparent", adjustcolor("midnightblue", 0.55))) h <- sun_hours(vh, date = "2026-12-21", lon = lonlat[1], lat = lonlat[2],                tz = "Antarctica/Davis", step = 10, convergence = lonlat[1]) attr(h, "daylight") #> [1] 24 summary(as.vector(h)) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs  #>   7.167  22.167  24.000  22.729  24.000  24.000  216775 ximage(h, extent = attr(h, "extent"), col = hcl.colors(64, "Inferno"), asp = 1, axes = FALSE)

title: Cast Shade and Sight Lines on Terrain
text: Viewshed: object-space visibility map. Around eye four 90 degree wedges azimuth. uses central (gnomonic) projection, straight edges stay straight, projected triangle still triangle. Triangles visited front back. grid, visiting quads order increasing row-plus-column offset eye already valid order, ’s sort. mesh, order topological sort one rule: across shared edge, triangle eye’s side goes first. Delaunay meshes never produce cycle; meshes can, cycles detected counted. Per narrow sector azimuth, horizon kept piecewise-linear upper envelope. triangle visible exactly rises horizon, raises. visible pieces map back ground convex polygons. horizon left end skyline. Shade: one directional sweep per sun position, linear number cells. “shadow surface” carried along light’s direction, dropping step * tan(elevation) per cell. cell shadow surface arriving ground. ’s longer write-lunashade’s docs/viewshed.md.

code: z <- volcano[nrow(volcano):1, ncol(volcano):1] ## vertices at cell centres, row by row from the north-west corner xy <- expand.grid(x = 2667400 + seq(5, 605, by = 10), y = 6479570 - seq(5, 865, by = 10)) nc <- ncol(z); nr <- nrow(z) q <- expand.grid(c = 1:(nc - 1), r = 1:(nr - 1)) tl <- (q$r - 1) * nc + q$c tri <- rbind(cbind(tl, tl + 1, tl + nc), cbind(tl + 1, tl + nc + 1, tl + nc)) v <- viewshed_mesh(xy$x, xy$y, as.vector(t(z)), tri, c(2667700, 6478900)) v$area #> [1] 39870.68
